title: I released an AI-driven RPG where generated NPCs, locations, items, and quests persist as actual game objects
author: Admirable_Flower_287
selftext:
I released an experimental AI-driven RPG.

The main idea is that AI-generated content is not treated as one-off text. NPCs, locations, items, quests, and other elements are generated as persistent game objects that remain in the world.

The AI handles dialogue, narration, situational interpretation, quest progression, and world flavor.

Meanwhile, the game system manages the RPG structure itself: inventory, equipment, party members, combat, saves, progression, and world state.

So an NPC is not just a paragraph generated for one scene. The NPC can stay in the world, be met again later, join the party, leave, and potentially be found again.

Locations are also stored in the world, and items are treated as real game objects that can be owned, equipped, sold, lost, and saved.

The game is still experimental and has rough edges, but I wanted to share it here because I think this is an interesting direction for AI game development: using AI not just to generate content, but to help drive a persistent RPG world.

I’m the developer, so this is self-promotion.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
Do you notice any interesting scenarios/runs during playtesting?

Your video just shows a typical text-heavy rpg experience. I mean, I wouldn't know if the content is indeed generated on the fly. 

The idea seems cool to me as a dev but I am not sure if players feel the same

replies.author: Admirable_Flower_287
replies.body: Yes, there are some interesting runs/scenarios, especially because the player can type free-form actions. A lot of the fun comes from the tension between what the player tries to do, what the world state allows, and how the GM/LLM interprets it. It can look like a text-heavy RPG in a short video, so I understand the concern. If you search “Instantale” on YouTube or X, you can find some third-party gameplay videos. Most are in Japanese, though.

comments.author: florodude
comments.body: I did the same thing when I had fable and it was a blast. I made a interactive text RPG like Zork, except you could type in any theme you wanted and it'd create the game for you, and use LLMs only when the verbs failed...it's pretty cool but I've got more polish I'm waiting on Fable for.

comments.author: Afraid_Test6461
comments.body: well done, what was the stack?

replies.author: Admirable_Flower_287
replies.body: Thanks! Mostly Python + Kivy for the game/client side. For LLMs, it supports llama.cpp / GGUF for local models, with optional OpenAI/Claude APIs.
